objective: V3.9.10 — Task-Frame Context: give agents the best context for the job they are doing right now — task frame first, supporting retrieval second.
context: V3.9.9 Context That Feeds (#56–#63) shipped retrieval transparency (inclusion_reason, slim sync, hygiene). Live QA showed hybrid retrieval alone does not answer what an agent needs in the moment — it surfaces handoff-shaped keyword matches, not a work brief. Mr. Go: context should follow the ticket and current work, not generic search.
decisions: Task frame is authoritative over retrieval: ticket detail + last handoff + constraints + decisions before supporting memories
Retrieval query derived from current ticket narrative (title, description, acceptance) — not generic AGENT_SYNC_QUERY alone
Supporting memories cap 3–4; prefer lesson, constraint, qa_result; exclude rows already in handoff timeline
Cursor and Codex get role-shaped frames (builder vs architect) from same engine
MEMORY_HIERARCHY authority order unchanged — filesystem and tickets outrank retrieval
One ticket at a time — claim, implement, QA, approve, close
Finish V3.9.9 (#62 UI/hygiene, #63 doc lock) before claiming V3.9.10 tickets
non_goals: Replacing tickets tab or handoff timeline with retrieval
Live model quality tuning in tests
risks: Task frame must not duplicate entire handoff prose into prompts
Ticket-derived queries must not pull stale unrelated handoffs via loose token overlap
UI reframe must not imply retrieval rows are priority truth
qa_expectations: CROWLEY_TEST_MODE=1 CROWLEY_EMBED_PROVIDER=off full unittest; task-frame fixture tests with assigned ticket #62/#63 scenarios; browser spot-check Agent Feed brief section; bus restart after API changes
next_action: Mr. Go approves packet; Codex mints with scripts/codex_sync.py --create-tickets tickets/v3.9.10_task_frame_context.json; Cursor claims first ticket only when directed

approval.note: Approved 2026-07-02 — task-frame context follow-on after V3.9.9 #62/#63.
